output.title: When opt-in records stop being trustworthy
output.body:
If your opt-in records stop being trustworthy, treat that as a workflow check before the next send, not as a broad AI project. The question is simple: can you tell, for each record, whether consent is current, withdrawn, or unclear? If you cannot, do not guess.

For a small business owner, this usually shows up as manual checking, a spreadsheet full of edge cases, or the uneasy habit of sending to a list because it is there. That is where the time leak starts. The approved persona scenario already includes repeated manual work; consent checks can join that same drag when the records are messy. The right move is not to automate the send first. It is to separate the records first.

One practical next step is to review one recent campaign and sort the contacts into three buckets: current, stale, and unknown. Route the stale and unknown group away from the send list until you have enough evidence to reclassify them. That can stay manual, live in a spreadsheet, or sit inside existing tooling if your system already keeps consent history or clean segments. If it does, use that as your first diagnostic. If it does not, a small workflow check in your own environment may be enough to show the gap.

Human approval should still sit in the loop for any send decision. Better a boring list review than a polite mistake.
